questions.question: Why must AI-generated finance narratives be reviewed carefully?
options: They can sound plausible while hiding weak data, wrong assumptions, or missing approvals
They use a different tone from the commentary the controlling team normally writes
They take longer to produce than the manual variance commentary they replace
They cannot reach the ledger directly, so every figure has to be typed in by hand
questions.explanation: Finance outputs require source traceability, visible assumptions, and approval controls. A fluent narrative is not evidence.

questions.question: An AI draft explains a budget variance using a figure that does not match the ledger. Which signal is that?
options: Source mismatch - the narrative and the underlying data disagree, so the source trace failed
Forecast uncertainty - the projection carries a range the narrative did not state clearly
Approval risk - the commentary was shared before the approval owner had reviewed it
Variance gap - a movement in the numbers was left without any explanation at all
questions.explanation: Source mismatch is the signal where the narrative and the source data disagree. The matching control is the source trace, which has to run before AI-assisted analysis is shared.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: An approval that releases the commentary into the management report
A ranked finance AI review plan with matched controls and rationale
An ERP integration that posts the corrected figures back to the ledger
A forecast whose confidence interval is guaranteed by the source data
questions.explanation: The artifact supports review and control selection. Approval owners remain accountable for what is released.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: A tone guide that keeps the commentary consistent with last quarter's report
A rule that variance below a threshold needs no explanation in the narrative
A shared drafting inbox where any controller can publish the final commentary directly
An assumption log that records what each figure assumed and why it was chosen
questions.explanation: An assumption log makes finance reasoning visible. Source trace, variance check, and a named approval owner are the other controls this lesson teaches.

questions.question: When should finance AI work require a launch gate?
options: Only when the commentary will be read outside the finance department
Only when the analysis covers a full year rather than a single month
Only when the model, rather than a controller, produced the first draft
When impact, uncertainty, and approval or source-trace risk are high
questions.explanation: High-risk finance workflows need explicit review before use, scaled to impact, uncertainty, and approval or source risk.

questions.question: What should variance explanations be linked to?
options: The evidence and the source data that each figure was drawn from
The tone and phrasing agreed for the management reporting pack
The assumptions the drafter used, whether or not they were reviewed
A reusable prompt that produces commentary in a consistent format
questions.explanation: Finance narratives should remain traceable to evidence. Assumptions must be logged and checked rather than carried forward unreviewed.
